calls.reasoning: Anchor is the Sep 4 close of $100.61 (Sep 7 is Labor Day; 8 trading days remain: Sep 8-11, 14-17). Over a horizon this short, a stock price is close to a martingale, so the reference class is 8-trading-day forward closes conditional on a fresh >15% earnings/guidance-cut gap down, and the prior is the last close with dispersion set by option-implied vol. Post-earnings IV has already crushed to 40.8%, implying sigma ~7.5% over 8 sessions (~$7.5), so the bulk of the distribution sits roughly $90-$111. I set the median at $100.0, a whisker below spot: post-announcement drift after a fourth guidance cut of the year, four sell-side targets now at or below spot (Piper $80, JPM $95, Wells $95, Stifel $100) and a fresh 52-week low at $97.99 argue mildly down, while a ~10x P/E, a $115.6 consensus target, short-term reversal after an 18% single-day drop, and a new CEO taking over Sep 8 argue mildly up - these roughly offset and neither is large next to the vol. Escape mass: below $75 needs a ~-25% move (~3.5 sigma), plausible only via a broad market break or another company disaster, priced 0.6%; above $130 needs ~+29%, with the one concrete mechanism being a takeover/LBO approach at an $11B depressed-valuation cap, priced 1.0%. Market check: no Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi contract on LULU's price exists, so there is no crowd anchor and no blending was done. Evidence is one-sided on fundamentals (deteriorating) but that is already in the price after a 17.4% repricing; I therefore stay near the random-walk base rate.

disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks the tie — PEAD after a guidance cut and one-day-loser reversal are both roughly 0.5-1.5% and offset. I take the reading I would bet on: median $100.0, i.e. the anchor less the lognormal median drag, with no meaningful directional tilt.
